outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot in which each marker is an individual sample (n = 141 samples), so individual data points are inherently displayed; scatter plots are exempt from requiring additional overlay of individual points.

Each marker is an individual cell-line/reporter combination plotted as mean ± s.d. with error bars; this is a scatter plot, which is exempt from the individual-data-points requirement (the points themselves are the individual measurements).

This panel shows fitted probability density (line) curves per subtype. Line plots are exempt from the individual-data-points requirement because overlaying raw points would make them unreadable; the underlying cell-line-level data are shown in panels A/B as noted in the caption.
This is a boxplot (exempt by default), and it additionally overlays individual sample points (pink/purple dots) on top of each box, so individual data points are explicitly shown.

Polar histograms display the distribution of phase differences over time for each cell line (color-coded), acting as a histogram/distribution plot rather than a simple bar chart of a single mean; this type is exempt from requiring overlaid individual points.

This polar histogram shows subtype-level averages across 1–4 cell line models. Although F itself does not overlay individual points, the underlying individual cell-line-level phase-difference distributions that were averaged are explicitly shown in panel E (cross-referenced in the caption), satisfying the need to show the individual data behind the average.
This is an illustrative line-plot example of a single signal fit (not an averaged summary statistic across samples), and line plots are exempt from the individual-data-points requirement.

Each marker represents an individual sample's fitted parameters (n = 117 samples) with error bars reflecting fit uncertainty; this is a scatter plot, which is exempt since the points themselves constitute the individual data.
